name: Neo-Victorian style

card.summary: A modern revival of Victorian dress and manners, with tailored waistcoats, high collars, corsetry and period grooming, used to build a distinctive, formal, period-inspired look.
card.note: A fashion aesthetic with overlaps in steampunk and gothic dress; not a grooming or medical method.

quick.overview:
Neo-Victorian style is a modern aesthetic that revives Victorian-era clothing, grooming and manners. It is used to create a formal, period-flavoured look, from waistcoats and high collars to corset-style silhouettes and carefully groomed facial hair.

It belongs to a wider cultural movement of nostalgia for the Victorian period, seen in literature, television and design. It overlaps with steampunk and gothic fashion.
quick.how: People assemble outfits from Victorian-inspired pieces such as tailored waistcoats, bowler hats, long skirts with bustle shapes, corsets worn as outerwear, brass-and-leather accessories, and grooming such as straight-razor shaving [1][2]. Some adopt period manners as well [1].
quick.risks: As clothing it carries no physical risks beyond those of the garments themselves. Tight corsetry is the main item people consider with care. The label is also used derisively in some political discussion [1].

lead: Neo-Victorianism is a contemporary cultural and aesthetic movement marked by overt nostalgia for and revivalism of the Victorian period [1]. In fashion it appears as a deliberate return to nineteenth-century silhouettes and details.

Adherents may wear Victorian-style clothing, adopt manners and habits such as straight-razor shaving, calling cards and wax-sealed letters, and furnish homes in period style [1]. The style overlaps with gothic fashion and is distinct from Japanese Lolita and Aristocrat fashions [1].

Steampunk fashion, which formed in the 1980s and 1990s alongside goth and punk, draws on mid-nineteenth-century silhouettes, brass goggles, bowler hats and corsets, and reached high fashion through designers such as John Galliano and Jean Paul Gaultier in the 2010s [2]. Neo-Victorian fiction and screen work, including Sherlock and Downton Abbey, has helped popularise the look [1].

chain: Wear Victorian-inspired tailoring and period grooming
Stand out with a cohesive, period-themed appearance
angle.text: People use neo-Victorian clothing and grooming to craft a recognisable, formal look. Waistcoats, high collars, tailored coats and groomed facial hair define the silhouette directly.

infobox: Waistcoats, bowler hats, corsets, bustle skirts [2]

paras: The style appears in everyday objects, furniture and clothing alike [1]. In dress, steampunk fashion offers its most developed vocabulary: bustles, conical or flared skirts, corsets as outerwear in brocade or leather, bowler hats and pith helmets, often mixed with punk, goth and burlesque elements [2].

Steampunk fashion took shape in the 1980s and 1990s, the first steampunk convention was held in 2006, and the first steampunk clothing company was founded in 2005; designers brought it to the runway in the 2010s [2]. Neo-Victorian fiction, such as John Fowles's The French Lieutenant's Woman and A. S. Byatt's Possession, and television such as Ripper Street helped build the broader movement [1].

The style is popular among some social conservatives in the US and UK, and the term is sometimes used derisively toward them [1]. Neo-Victorian studies is an established academic field with its own peer-reviewed journal [1].

timeline.event: Steampunk fashion forms alongside goth and punk [2].
Steampunk Couture, reported as the first steampunk clothing company, is founded [2].
The first steampunk convention, SalonCon, is held [2].
Designers such as Galliano and Gaultier bring the style to high fashion [2].
